text: What does the Weak Supplementation principle, PP(x,y) → ∃z(P(z,y) ∧ ¬O(z,x)), rule out?
choices: A whole that has exactly one proper part and no remainder
explanation: WSP demands that whenever x is a proper part of y, some part of y is disjoint from x — a remainder — which forbids the pathological model where y has a single proper part and nothing else. It does not ban infinite parthood, atoms, or scattered fusions, all of which classical mereology permits.
